/**
 * @file observe.ts — pooled IntersectionObserver.
 *
 * Why it exists: project pages mount ~125 media figures plus ~30
 * carousels, and each one used to own a dedicated IntersectionObserver —
 * 200+ observer instances whose intersections the compositor recomputes
 * on every scroll frame (`computeIntersections` showed ~0.6s of a 6s
 * mobile scroll trace). Chromium's IO cost scales with observer COUNT ×
 * targets, so pooling every same-config observer into ONE instance cuts
 * the recompute to a handful of observers while each component keeps its
 * private observe/disconnect lifecycle.
 *
 * Pooling rule: observers are shared per (root, rootMargin, threshold)
 * config key within one IntersectionObserver implementation — pools are
 * WeakMap-keyed on the class itself so test doubles never dispatch
 * through a stale real-IO instance. Non-default roots are rare and
 * can't share an instance — those fall back to a dedicated
 * IntersectionObserver transparently.
 *
 * Dispatch: the pooled observer's single callback re-groups each entry
 * batch by owning handle, so every consumer sees exactly the callback
 * shape of a private IntersectionObserver.
 */
 
import { TYPE_STRINGS } from '@core/tokens/strings/types.js'
import { SCROLL_SETTLE } from '@core/tokens/motion/scroll.js'
import { WINDOW_EVENTS } from '@core/tokens/events/dom.js'
 
/**
 * Pooled-observer options — IntersectionObserverInit plus the pool-only
 * `pauseOnScroll` flag: when set, the shared observer disconnects for the
 * duration of a scroll gesture and re-observes every target at settle
 * (Chromium re-delivers current intersections on observe, so consumers
 * get the same entries they would have seen live — just deferred to a
 * frame where the budget exists). Cutting every target out of the
 * engine's per-frame intersection pass removes the computeIntersections
 * + forced-layout-sync cost a mobile trace measured at ~1s over a 6s
 * fling. Ignored on the dedicated-observer fallback (non-default root).
 */
export interface PooledObserveOptions extends IntersectionObserverInit {
  /** Disconnect the pool while scrolling; re-observe targets at settle. */
  pauseOnScroll?: boolean
}
 
/** Minimal observer surface components consume — a real
 *  IntersectionObserver structurally satisfies it, so fields can hold
 *  either a pooled handle or a dedicated observer. `callback` mirrors
 *  happy-dom's IO surface so tests can dispatch entries directly —
 *  browsers don't expose it, hence optional. */
export interface ObserverHandle {
  /** Starts observing `el` under this handle's callback. */
  observe(el: Element): void
  /** Stops observing `el` for this handle only. */
  unobserve(el: Element): void
  /** Removes every element this handle observes; the pooled observer
   *  stays live for other handles sharing the config. */
  disconnect(): void
  /** Consumer callback — exposed for test-driven entry dispatch. */
  callback?: IntersectionObserverCallback
}
 
/** One consumer's registration inside a pooled observer. */
interface PoolHandle {
  /** Consumer callback — invoked with this handle's entries only. */
  callback: IntersectionObserverCallback
  /** Elements this handle currently watches (for scoped disconnect). */
  targets: Set<Element>
}
 
/** A shared IntersectionObserver plus the element→handles routing map. */
interface PoolEntry {
  /** The single real IntersectionObserver behind all handles. */
  io: IntersectionObserver
  /** Element → set of handles watching it (an element may be observed
   *  by several handles in the same config pool). */
  owners: Map<Element, Set<PoolHandle>>
  /** False while the pool is scroll-paused: observe() registrations are
   *  kept in `owners` but held off the real IO until scroll settle. */
  live: boolean
}
 
/** Config-keyed observer pools — one Map per IntersectionObserver
 *  implementation (WeakMap so a swapped-in test double starts with fresh
 *  pools instead of dispatching through a stale instance). */
const pools = new WeakMap<typeof IntersectionObserver, Map<string, PoolEntry>>()
 
/** Pools created with `pauseOnScroll` — tracked per IO implementation
 *  (same WeakMap discipline as `pools`) so scroll transitions can
 *  disconnect/re-observe them without touching live-gated pools. */
const pauseablePools = new WeakMap<typeof IntersectionObserver, Set<PoolEntry>>()
 
/** The scroll listener is installed lazily on the first
 *  pauseable pool — pages with no pauseable observers pay nothing. */
let scrollPauseHooked = false
 
/** True while pauseable pools are disconnected for a scroll gesture. */
let poolsPaused = false
 
/** Pending resume — reset by every scroll event so pools only come back
 *  after the gesture is truly quiet. */
let resumeTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null
 
/**
 * The scroll-state flag flickers under throttled input — scroll events
 * arrive in bursts spaced past a short debounce, so a pause keyed to the
 * isScrolling transition churns pools through disconnect/re-observe
 * cycles that each re-deliver every target's entries mid-fling. Pools
 * instead hold until the event stream goes quiet for the shared settle
 * window — the same window the scroll-state debounce waits for, so the
 * flag and the pools now agree on when a gesture ends.
 */
const POOL_RESUME_QUIET_MS = SCROLL_SETTLE.QUIET_MS
 
/**
 * Builds the pool key for a config. Numbers stringify stably; threshold
 * arrays join in order (callers always pass canonical order).
 * @param options — IntersectionObserver init
 * @returns opaque key uniquely identifying the shared pool
 */
const configKey = (options?: PooledObserveOptions): string =>
  `${options?.pauseOnScroll ? 'p' : ''}|${options?.rootMargin ?? ''}|${Array.isArray(options?.threshold) ? options.threshold.join(',') : (options?.threshold ?? '')}`
 
/**
 * Re-observes every target in every paused pool — the engine re-delivers
 * each element's current intersection on the next frame, so consumers
 * see the same entries they would have received live. Registrations go
 * through the same budgeted drain as dispatch: ~180 observe() calls +
 * the engine's compute pass in one frame was a recurring post-scroll
 * frame drop, so the burst spreads across a few frames instead.
 */
const resumePools = (): void => {
  poolsPaused = false
 
  resumeTimer = null
 
  const set = pauseablePools.get(IntersectionObserver)
 
  if (!set) return
 
  set.forEach((pool) => {
    pool.live = true
 
    pool.owners.forEach((_handles, el) => enqueueDispatch(() => pool.io.observe(el)))
  })
 
  // Kick unconditionally — drainDispatch is idempotent: when a prior
  // continuation is armed this just drains the merged queue inline and
  // the stale rAF lands on an empty queue.
  drainDispatch()
}
 
/**
 * Passive scroll listener for pauseable pools: the first event of a
 * gesture disconnects every flagged pool (targets stay in `owners` —
 * lifecycle bookkeeping is untouched); each following event resets the
 * quiet-window timer so the pools stay offline until the gesture truly
 * ends, immune to the bursty delivery that flickers the isScrolling flag.
 */
const handlePoolScroll = (): void => {
  const set = pauseablePools.get(IntersectionObserver)
 
  if (set) {
    if (!poolsPaused) {
      poolsPaused = true
 
      set.forEach((pool) => {
        pool.io.disconnect()
 
        pool.live = false
      })
    }
 
    if (resumeTimer) clearTimeout(resumeTimer)
 
    resumeTimer = setTimeout(resumePools, POOL_RESUME_QUIET_MS)
  }
}
 
/**
 * Lazily wires the pool scroll listener — the first pauseable pool
 * installs the one module-level passive listener.
 */
const ensureScrollPauseHook = (): void => {
  if (scrollPauseHooked) return
 
  scrollPauseHooked = true
 
  if (typeof window !== TYPE_STRINGS.UNDEFINED) {
    window.addEventListener(WINDOW_EVENTS.SCROLL, handlePoolScroll, { passive: true })
  }
}
 
/**
 * Per-frame work budget for dispatch drains. Post-scroll resume
 * re-delivers every watched element's state in one batch (~180 consumer
 * callbacks on media-heavy routes — media attaches, video gates,
 * reveal triggers) and running them back-to-back once produced a ~170ms
 * frame. Small batches still flush synchronously inside the IO callback
 * (spec-async delivery already tolerates a task boundary); only work
 * past the budget defers to the next frame.
 */
const DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS = 4
 
/** Consumer callbacks queued for the budgeted drain, FIFO per batch. */
const dispatchQueue: Array<() => void> = []
 
/** Pending rAF continuation while queued callbacks remain past budget. */
let dispatchRaf = 0
 
/**
 * Runs queued consumer callbacks inline until the frame budget is spent,
 * then continues on rAF — keeps delivery near-synchronous for live
 * traffic while spreading settle bursts across frames.
 */
const drainDispatch = (): void => {
  dispatchRaf = 0
 
  const t0 = performance.now()
 
  let i = 0
 
  // Bounded drain loop, not traversal stack emulation: consumes the
  // batch queue until the frame budget is spent (pushing happens only in
  // enqueueDispatch, never here — callbacks queued mid-drain ride the
  // same pass while budget remains).
  while (i < dispatchQueue.length && performance.now() - t0 < DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS) {
    dispatchQueue[i++]()
  }
 
  dispatchQueue.splice(0, i)
 
  if (dispatchQueue.length) {
    dispatchRaf = requestAnimationFrame(drainDispatch)
  }
}
 
/**
 * Enqueues one consumer callback invocation; the caller kicks the inline
 * drain once per batch so the budget spans the batch, not each callback.
 * @param fn — the bound handle.callback(bucket, io) call
 */
const enqueueDispatch = (fn: () => void): void => {
  dispatchQueue.push(fn)
}
 
/**
 * Routes a pooled callback batch to the owning handles: entries are
 * grouped per handle so each consumer's callback receives only the
 * entries for elements it registered — same contract as a private IO.
 * Invocations go through the budgeted queue so settle bursts spread.
 * @param pool — the shared pool whose handles to dispatch to
 * @param entries — raw entry batch from the pooled observer
 * @param io — the pooled observer (forwarded as the callback's second arg)
 */
const dispatch = (
  pool: PoolEntry,
  entries: IntersectionObserverEntry[],
  io: IntersectionObserver
): void => {
  const byHandle = new Map<PoolHandle, IntersectionObserverEntry[]>()
 
  for (const entry of entries) {
    const handles = pool.owners.get(entry.target)
 
    if (!handles) continue
 
    for (const handle of handles) {
      let bucket = byHandle.get(handle)
 
      if (!bucket) {
        bucket = []
 
        byHandle.set(handle, bucket)
      }
 
      bucket.push(entry)
    }
  }
 
  for (const [handle, bucket] of byHandle) enqueueDispatch(() => handle.callback(bucket, io))
 
  if (!dispatchRaf) drainDispatch()
}
 
/**
 * Detaches `handle` from `el` inside `pool`: removes the routing entry
 * and unobserves the element only when no other handle watches it.
 * @param pool — shared pool holding the element registration
 * @param handle — the consuming handle detaching
 * @param el — element to stop watching for this handle
 */
const release = (pool: PoolEntry, handle: PoolHandle, el: Element): void => {
  const handles = pool.owners.get(el)
 
  if (handles) {
    handles.delete(handle)
 
    if (!handles.size) {
      pool.owners.delete(el)
 
      pool.io.unobserve(el)
 
      // Last target gone — tear the pooled observer down entirely so a
      // drained pool holds no live registrations.
      if (!pool.owners.size) pool.io.disconnect()
    }
  }
 
  handle.targets.delete(el)
}
 
/**
 * Creates an observer backed by the shared pool when possible.
 * Falls back to a dedicated IntersectionObserver when the API is absent
 * or a non-default `root` is requested (roots can't be shared).
 * @param callback — consumer callback, same signature as IntersectionObserver's
 * @param options — IntersectionObserver init (root must be default for pooling)
 * @returns observer handle with observe/unobserve/disconnect
 */
export function observeIntersection(
  callback: IntersectionObserverCallback,
  options?: PooledObserveOptions
): ObserverHandle {
  if (typeof IntersectionObserver === TYPE_STRINGS.UNDEFINED || options?.root) {
    return new IntersectionObserver(callback, options)
  }
 
  const key = configKey(options)
 
  let byConfig = pools.get(IntersectionObserver)
 
  if (!byConfig) {
    byConfig = new Map()
 
    pools.set(IntersectionObserver, byConfig)
  }
 
  let pool = byConfig.get(key)
 
  if (!pool) {
    const entry: PoolEntry = {
      owners: new Map(),
      io: null as unknown as IntersectionObserver,
      // A pauseable pool created mid-gesture starts paused — its
      // registrations queue in `owners` until the quiet window lapses.
      live: !(options?.pauseOnScroll && poolsPaused),
    }
 
    entry.io = new IntersectionObserver((entries, io) => dispatch(entry, entries, io), options)
 
    byConfig.set(key, entry)
 
    pool = entry
 
    if (options?.pauseOnScroll) {
      ensureScrollPauseHook()
 
      let pauseable = pauseablePools.get(IntersectionObserver)
 
      if (!pauseable) {
        pauseable = new Set()
 
        pauseablePools.set(IntersectionObserver, pauseable)
      }
 
      pauseable.add(entry)
    }
  }
 
  const handle: PoolHandle = { callback, targets: new Set() }
 
  return {
    callback,
    observe(el: Element): void {
      if (handle.targets.has(el)) return
 
      handle.targets.add(el)
 
      let handles = pool.owners.get(el)
 
      if (!handles) {
        handles = new Set()
 
        pool.owners.set(el, handles)
      }
 
      handles.add(handle)
 
      // While the pool is scroll-paused the registration stays in
      // `owners` only — settle re-observes every queued target.
      if (pool.live) {
        pool.io.observe(el)
      }
    },
    unobserve(el: Element): void {
      release(pool, handle, el)
    },
    disconnect(): void {
      for (const el of handle.targets) release(pool, handle, el)
 
      handle.targets.clear()
    },
  }
}
